text: ICE pays counties and cities to hold people in their jails under agreements with each one. Those payments are not in federal spending data: USAspending shows ICE paying 37 local governments a combined $2.62 million in fiscal years 2023 to 2026, mostly for things like parking and services.
What ICE repays the Bureau of Prisons for holding people moves between agencies and does not appear as contracts. GAO reports the prisons send their extra staffing costs to ICE for repayment.

Both budget laws fund 287(g) agreements with local police, but no ICE grant or payment to a 287(g) partner appears in federal spending data. ICE's only grant in fiscal years 2023 to 2026 was $0.9 million to a children's safety charity.

Since September 2025 ICE has offered 287(g) partners repayment of officers' salaries and benefits, up to $100,000 per agency for vehicles, and $500 to $1,000 per officer each quarter. FWD.us estimates that up to $2 billion has been promised; agencies in Florida had received nearly $40 million. Which agencies are paid, and how much, is not published.
source: NPR, May 2026 (citing DHS, FWD.us and Florida state records)
